sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The rapid growth of India’s digital economy, anchored by the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and cheap mobile data, has turned the nation into a global blueprint for digital financial inclusion. By building a public digital infrastructure, the state has democratized electronic payments, allowing street vendors and major corporations alike to operate on the exact same interoperable network. This digital pivot has formalized large sectors of the informal economy, expanded fintech innovation, and streamlined direct benefit transfers, cutting out corruption. However, this sudden transition introduces severe economic vulnerabilities, notably an alarming escalation in sophisticated cyber-fraud and digital phishing operations targeting newly connected, digitally illiterate populations. Furthermore, the rapid growth of fintech lenders using predatory automated algorithms risks driving low-income borrowers into deep debt traps through high-interest short-term loans. The long-term stability of India's digital marketplace depends on implementing strong data protection laws, enforcing strict algorithm auditing for fintech firms, and launching massive public digital literacy campaigns.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The escalating global water security crisis is often misdiagnosed as a simple challenge of climate-induced scarcity, when it is heavily compounded by systemic mismanagement and misallocated resources. Globally, critical freshwater aquifers are being rapidly depleted by industrial-scale agriculture, driven by inefficient flood irrigation and state-subsidized groundwater extraction. This policy-driven depletion is worsened by widespread industrial pollution and untreated municipal sewage, which turns vital river systems into toxic channels and shrinks the global supply of potable water. Legacy water governance models remain stubbornly centralized, focusing on massive, capital-intensive dams and long-distance water transfer projects that disrupt river ecology and displace marginalized communities. Mitigating this existential threat requires decentralized water governance, centering on localized rainwater harvesting, wastewater recycling, and watershed rejuvenation. Furthermore, agriculture must pivot toward micro-irrigation and crop diversification away from water-intensive cash crops in arid regions. True water security requires treating water not as a commodified, infinite economic input, but as a finite, shared ecological asset that must be protected.

questions.q: India's public digital infrastructure is credited with transforming the economy by
opts: shutting down informal street vending to protect large corporations
democratizing electronic payments across both informal and corporate sectors
forcing all fintech innovations under state-owned monopolies
eliminating the need for data protection laws
questions.why: Street vendors and corporations use “the exact same interoperable network”. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the text, a direct benefit of formalising the informal economy through digital tools is
opts: the complete eradication of automated lending algorithms
streamlining direct benefit transfers and reducing corruption
eliminating the need for digital literacy campaigns
reducing the market share of major payment providers
questions.why: Stated in the third sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author warns that newly connected, digitally illiterate populations are particularly vulnerable to
opts: strict data protection enforcement by the state
questions.why: Stated in the fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: A major risk of automated fintech lending algorithms, per the passage, is that they can
opts: block low-income borrowers from electronic payments
drop interest rates so low that banks fail
drive low-income borrowers into debt traps through predatory short-term loans
questions.why: Stated in the fifth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author concludes that the lasting success of India's digital marketplace requires
opts: phasing out UPI and returning to cash
strong data laws, algorithm audits and mass digital literacy campaigns
restricting digital access to educated urban users
questions.why: The last sentence lists all three. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author says the water crisis is “misdiagnosed” when it is blamed entirely on
questions.why: First sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the text, a major policy-driven factor speeding up aquifer depletion is
opts: crop diversification away from cash crops
state-subsidised groundwater extraction and inefficient flood irrigation
questions.why: Second sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The passage criticises legacy water governance for prioritising
opts: large, expensive dams and transfer projects that damage river ecology
micro-irrigation subsidies that exclude small farmers
questions.why: Fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: To achieve water security, the author says agriculture must
opts: pump more groundwater with power subsidies
move to micro-irrigation and away from water-heavy crops in dry zones
shift entirely to water-intensive cash crops
questions.why: Sixth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The final sentence asks society to view water as
opts: an infinite input to be commodified
a secondary resource for industry to manage
an unmanageable asset because of climate
a finite, shared ecological asset that must be protected
questions.why: Last sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Identify the clause type: “Whatever he says does not matter.”
questions.why: The clause is the subject of 'does not matter', so it is a noun clause. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech: He said, “I am busy today.”
opts: He said that he was busy that day.
He said that I am busy today.
He said that he is busy today.
He said that he had been busy today.
questions.why: Present becomes past; 'today' becomes 'that day'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the correct sentence:
opts: He is taller than me am.
He is taller than I am.
He is taller than I am tall.
questions.why: 'Than I am': subject pronoun with the verb. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Find the error: “The results of the survey was surprising.”
questions.why: The subject is 'results' (plural): 'were'. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: “He is ____ honest man.”
questions.why: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (silent h). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The 'Districts as Export Hubs' initiative expanded in September 2026 to cover more than:
The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article:
questions.why: C. P. Radhakrishnan is the 15th Vice-President.

questions.q: Anandkumar Velkumar won silver in the men's 1,000-m sprint at the 2026 World Games of which sport, held in Paraguay?
questions.why: World Skating Games. Oct 2026.

questions.q: Indian Air Force Day is observed on:
questions.why: The IAF was founded on 8 October 1932.

questions.q: The government grant announced at the Goa Chess Academy launch (2026) supports a chess tournament named after:
questions.why: ₹20 lakh for the Manohar Parrikar Chess Tournament.

questions.q: INS Nipun, the second Nistar-class diving support vessel, was commissioned in September 2026 at:
The seventh Global Fintech Fest was held in 2026 in:
In 2026 the Ministry of AYUSH signed an MoU with which body for AI-driven innovation in traditional medicine?
Who was crowned Miss Universe India 2026?
The chemical symbol for sodium is:
questions.why: From the Latin 'natrium'.

questions.q: Today is Monday. After 61 days it will be:
questions.why: 61 = 8 weeks + 5 days; Monday + 5 = Saturday. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: Two trains run in opposite directions with speeds 2 : 1. The first passes a standing man in 5 s, the second in 8 s. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.why: Lengths 10v and 8v; relative speed 3v; 18v ÷ 3v = 6 s. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: Who is the fastest of Rani, Supriya and Amita (all different)? I. Rani and Supriya take 5 days; Supriya and Amita take 10 days. II. Rani and Amita take 30/7 days.
questions.why: From I, r − a = 1/10, so Rani beats Amita. Since s + a = 1/10, s is below 1/10 while r is above it, so Rani is fastest. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: Ten years ago Sitamma was three times Radha's age. In ten years she will be twice Radha's age. What is the ratio of their present ages?
Identify the next term: A1Z, B3Y, D6X, G10W, K15V, …
questions.why: Letters +1, +2, +3, +4, +5 → P; numbers +2, +3, +4, +5, +6 → 21; last letters run back to U. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Raju walks 20 m west, turns left and walks 20 m, turns left and walks 20 m, turns left again and walks 20 m. Which direction is he facing?
questions.why: West → left = South → left = East → left = North. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: If REASON is coded 5 and BELIEVED 7, what is the code for GOVERNMENT?
questions.why: Code = number of letters − 1: GOVERNMENT has 10, so 9. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: In a row of boys, Seby is 20th from the left and Alan 22nd from the right. When they swap, 18 boys are to the right of Alan. How many boys are in the row?
questions.why: After the swap Alan is 20th from the left with 18 to his right: 20 + 18 = 38. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Ichthyology : Fishes :: Pedology : ?
questions.why: Pedology is the study of soil. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Find the number in place of ?: 1, 7, 37, 187, 937, ?
questions.why: × 5 + 2 each time: 937 × 5 + 2 = 4687. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: According to Hahnemann, emotional diseases of recent origin produced and kept up by the mind (§226) may be cured by:
opts: psychological means such as confidence, friendly advice and reasoning
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Psychotherapeutic measures, with a suitable antipsoric regimen afterwards.

questions.q: In chronic diseases (§259–261) Hahnemann advised the patient to avoid:
opts: medicinal substances in food and drink, such as strong coffee, spices and perfumes
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. They disturb the action of the remedy.

questions.q: Kent's second prescription may be any of the following EXCEPT:
opts: a repetition of the first remedy
a mixture of several remedies given together
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Kent listed repetition, antidote, complementary remedy and change of plan; mixtures go against the simplex principle.

questions.q: Complaints from exposure to damp cold, especially when hot days are followed by cold nights, call for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Dulcamara: diarrhoea, rheumatism and skin complaints from damp cold.

questions.q: Prolapse of the uterus with bearing-down sensation as if everything would come out, crossing the legs for relief, with indifference to family, indicates:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Sepia: bearing down, indifference to loved ones.

questions.q: Hurried, busy feeling, bearing-down pelvic pains, and the need to keep busy to suppress sexual feelings point to:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Lilium: hurry, wild feeling, uterine prolapse with cardiac symptoms.

questions.q: Cramps in calves and toes, epileptic spasms, and complaints relieved by drinking cold water point to:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Cuprum: violent cramps, cold water relieves the cough.

questions.q: Which of these is prepared from a diseased tissue or product (a nosode)?
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Thyroidinum is a sarcode; Lac caninum and Sepia are animal sources.

questions.q: In homoeopathic pharmacy, the 'drug strength' of a mother tincture describes:
opts: the proportion of the crude drug in the mother tincture
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Usually 1/10 for most tinctures under the new method.

questions.q: Which repertory method gives most importance to the patient's general modalities and concomitants rather than mental symptoms?
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Boenninghausen's method relies on generalised modalities and concomitants.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, a general aggravation from cold air is looked up in the chapter:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Modalities affecting the whole patient are in Generalities.

questions.q: A patient understands speech but cannot speak fluently after a stroke. The lesion is in:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Broca's (areas 44, 45) = motor speech; Wernicke's lesion gives fluent but meaningless speech.

questions.q: Erythropoietin is produced mainly by the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. In response to hypoxia.

questions.q: Rheumatic fever is a complication of infection with:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Usually after a streptococcal sore throat.

questions.q: Microcytic hypochromic anaemia is most often due to:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Commonest anaemia in India.

questions.q: Heat intolerance, weight loss with good appetite, tremor and exophthalmos suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Thyroid overactivity.

questions.q: The main dietary advice for a patient with gout is to reduce intake of:
opts: purine-rich foods such as organ meats and alcohol
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Purines raise uric acid.

questions.q: Palpitation, headache and a bursting sensation in the head from exposure to the sun suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Glonoine: sunstroke, surging of blood to the head.

questions.q: The average duration of a normal pregnancy from the first day of the last menstrual period is:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. 40 weeks.

questions.q: Severe acute malnutrition in a child of 6–59 months is identified by a mid-upper arm circumference below:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Or bilateral pitting oedema, or weight-for-height below −3 SD.

questions.q: The first aid for a person with a suspected spinal injury is to:
opts: keep the spine still and move only with proper support
bend the neck forward to open the airway
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Use jaw thrust instead of head tilt if needed.

questions.q: Inflammation of the paranasal sinuses with facial pain and nasal discharge is called:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Maxillary sinus is most often involved.

questions.q: Genus epidemicus is used in outbreak control to:
opts: find a common remedy for most cases in an epidemic
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Found by studying the symptoms of several cases.

questions.q: The crude birth rate is expressed per:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Live births in a year per 1,000 mid-year population.

questions.q: A post-mortem examination ordered by the police or magistrate in a suspicious death is called a:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Done under the BNSS (formerly CrPC) to establish cause and manner of death.
